title: K002: Add SSE event injection and configurable state
description:
**Size:** 📦 medium
**Category:** testing
**Priority:** high
**Source:** Proposed for 'With the latest commits/features, E2E tests were added'

Three additions to test/e2e/mockapi/mockapi.go: (1) SSE Event Injection — add broadcast channel slice to Server struct for connected SSE clients, modify existing SSE handler to register/deregister clients on fan-out list, implement POST /test/inject-event that accepts {event_type, payload} JSON, wraps in SSE wire format, broadcasts to all connected clients. (2) Configurable State — add mutable StateResponse field to Server (sync.RWMutex-protected), implement POST /test/configure-state that replaces the active state fixture at runtime, modify handleState to read from mutable fixture instead of hardcoded default. (3) State Fixture Enrichment — extend default StateResponse with SigningKeys (current + previous pub keys), BridgeConfig{Enabled: false}, RelayConfig{Sessions: []}, UserAccessConfig{Enabled: false}, IngressConfig{Enabled: false}, SiteToSiteConfig{Enabled: false}, 2 sample Data entries, 1 sample SecretRef.

**Rationale:** The SSE stream currently only emits node_state_updated while the agent handles 25 event types — there's no way to test execution flows (action_request → ack → result) or other event-driven behaviors. The state fixture lacks SigningKeys, BridgeConfig, RelayConfig, and other fields, so reconciliation code paths for these features are never exercised. Configurable state enables test scripts to set up specific scenarios without rebuilding the mock.

**Affected Areas:**
- test/e2e/mockapi/mockapi.go

implementation_notes:
Architecture: The Server struct gains 3 new field groups: (1) SSE broadcast — `sseClients []chan []byte` + `sseMu sync.Mutex` for client fan-out, (2) Mutable state — `stateFixture api.StateResponse` + `stateMu sync.RWMutex` for configurable state, (3) Inject counter — `injectCount atomic.Int64`. The broadcast uses buffered channels (cap 16) with non-blocking sends to avoid slow-client back-pressure blocking the injector. The state fixture is initialized with defaultStateFixture() in New() and replaced atomically via setState(). handleState switches from inline construction to getState() read. handleEvents adds a broadcast channel case to its select loop alongside keep-alive and context-done. Key patterns from codebase: sync.RWMutex usage in internal/api/client.go (SetAuthToken/getAuthToken) and internal/api/verifier.go (SetKeys/Verify) — same Lock/Unlock, RLock/RUnlock pattern. Atomic counters follow existing atomic.Int64 pattern. SSE wire format follows existing handleEvents: 'id: %s
event: %s
data: %s

'. Risks: (1) Slow SSE client could fill channel buffer — mitigated by non-blocking send with select/default. (2) State fixture is copied on each read — acceptable for test server. (3) Enriched fixture changes existing test assertions for Data/SecretRefs length — TestState_ReturnsFixturePeersAndPolicies must be updated from expecting 0 to expecting 2/1.
